tools.name: d1-create-database
tools.description: Create D1 Database — Create a new D1 database in your account.

jurisdiction.description: Specify the location to restrict the D1 database to run and store data. If this option is present, the location hint is ignored.

primary_location_hint.description: Specify the region to create the D1 primary, if available. If this option is omitted, the D1 will be created as close as possible to the current user.

tools.name: d1-delete-database

tools.name: d1-export-database
tools.description:
Export D1 Database as SQL — Export the SQL contents of a D1 database and return a URL where they can be downloaded. Note: this process may take
some time for larger DBs, during which your D1 will be unavailable to serve queries. To avoid
blocking your DB unnecessarily

current_bookmark.description: To poll an in-progress export, provide the current bookmark (returned by your first polling response)

no_data.description: Export only the table definitions, not their contents

no_schema.description: Export only each table's contents, not its definition

tables.description: Filter the export to just one or more tables. Passing an empty array is the same as not passing anything and means: export all tables.

output_format.description: Specifies that you will poll this endpoint until the export completes

tools.name: d1-get-database
tools.description: Get D1 Database — Get details for a specific D1 database.

fields.description:
Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response. When omitted,
all fields are returned.

tools.name: d1-import-database
tools.description:
Import SQL into your D1 Database — Generate a temporary URL for uploading an SQL file to, then instruct the D1 to import it
and poll it for status updates. Imports block the D1 for their duration.

action.description: Indicates you have a new SQL file to upload.

etag.description: Required when action is 'init' or 'ingest'. An md5 hash of the file you're uploading. Used to check if it already exists, and validate its contents before ingesting.

action.description: Indicates you've finished uploading to tell the D1 to start consuming it

etag.description: An md5 hash of the file you're uploading. Used to check if it already exists, and validate its contents before ingesting.

filename.description: The filename you have successfully uploaded.

action.description: Indicates you've finished uploading to tell the D1 to start consuming it

current_bookmark.description: This identifies the currently-running import, checking its status.

tools.name: d1-list-databases
tools.description: List D1 Databases — List D1 databases in your account.

name.description: a database name to search for.

tools.name: d1-query-database
tools.description: Query D1 Database — Execute a SQL query against a D1 database and return results as objects.

tools.name: d1-raw-database-query
tools.description: Raw D1 Database query — Execute a SQL query against a D1 database and return result rows as arrays rather than objects. This is a performance-optimized version of the /query endpoint.

tools.name: d1-time-travel-get-bookmark
tools.description:
Get D1 database bookmark — Retrieve the current bookmark, or the nearest bookmark at or before a provided timestamp.
Bookmarks can be used with the restore endpoint to revert the database to a previous point in time.

timestamp.description: An optional ISO 8601 timestamp. If provided, returns the nearest available bookmark at or before this timestamp. If omitted, returns the current bookmark.

tools.name: d1-time-travel-restore
tools.description:
Restore D1 Database to a bookmark or point in time — Restore a D1 database to a previous point in time either via a bookmark or a timestamp.
 — DESTRUCTIVE: This reverts the D1 database to a previous point in time. Data written after the bookmark will be lost.

bookmark.description: A bookmark to restore the database to. Required if `timestamp` is not provided.

timestamp.description: An ISO 8601 timestamp to restore the database to. Required if `bookmark` is not provided.

tools.name: telemetry_query
tools.description: Run a query — Run a temporary or saved query.

chart.description: When true, includes time-series data in the response.

chartType.description: Controls the SQL shape and response payload for the 'calculations' view. Omitted or 'timeseries_and_aggregate': current behaviour — both the time-series and aggregate queries. 'timeseries': time-series only. 'aggregate': aggregate only. 'di

compare.description: When true, includes a comparison dataset from the previous time period of equal length.

distributionScale.description: Value-axis bucketing for chartType 'distribution'. Omitted or 'log': geometric buckets, best for heavy-tailed latency. 'linear': fixed-width buckets, clearer for narrow or additive ranges. Ignored for other chartTypes. The response echoes t

dry.description: When true, executes the query without persisting the results. Useful for validation or previewing.

granularity.description: Number of time-series buckets. Only used when view is 'calculations'. Omit to let the system auto-detect an appropriate granularity.

ignoreSeries.description: When true, omits time-series data from the response and returns only aggregated values. Reduces response size when series are not needed.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return when view is 'events'. Also controls the number of group-by rows when view is 'calculations'.

offset.description: Cursor for pagination in event, trace, invocation, and agent views. Pass the $metadata.id of the last event, the trace cursor, or AgentRun.id to fetch the next page.

offsetBy.description: Numeric offset for paginating grouped/pattern results (top-N lists). Use together with limit. Not used by cursor-based pagination.

offsetDirection.description: Pagination direction: 'next' for forward, 'prev' for backward.

parameters.description: Query parameters defining what data to retrieve — filters, calculations, group-bys, and ordering. In practice this should always be provided for ad-hoc queries. Only omit when executing a previously saved query by queryId. Use the keys and

calculations.description: Aggregation calculations to compute (e.g. count, avg, p99). Each calculation produces aggregate values and optional time-series data.

datasets.description: Datasets to query. Leave empty to query all available datasets.

filterCombination.description: Logical operator for combining top-level filters: 'and' (all must match) or 'or' (any must match). Defaults to 'and'.

filters.description: Filters to narrow query results. Use the keys and values endpoints to discover available fields before building filters. Supports nested groups via kind: 'group'. Maximum nesting depth is 4.

groupBys.description: Fields to group calculation results by. Only applicable when the query view is 'calculations'. Produces per-group aggregate values.

havings.description: Post-aggregation filters applied to calculation results. Use to filter groups after aggregation (e.g. only groups where count > 100).

limit.description: Maximum number of group-by rows to return in calculation results. A value of 10 is a sensible default for most use cases.

needle.description: Full-text search expression applied across all event fields. Matches events containing the specified text.

orderBy.description: Ordering for grouped calculation results. Only effective when a group-by is present.

queryId.description: Identifier for the query. When parameters are omitted, this ID is used to load a previously saved query's parameters. When providing parameters inline, pass any identifier (e.g. an ad-hoc ID).

timeframe.description: Timeframe for the query using Unix timestamps in milliseconds. 'from' must be earlier than 'to'. Narrower timeframes produce faster responses and more specific results.

from.description: Start timestamp for the query timeframe. Unix timestamp in milliseconds

to.description: End timestamp for the query timeframe. Unix timestamp in milliseconds

view.description: Controls the shape of the response. 'events': individual log lines matching the query. 'calculations': aggregated metrics (count, avg, p99, etc.) with optional group-by breakdowns and time-series. 'invocations': events grouped by request ID
